# dsh-exit-code-lens
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that stops the agent from "investigating" commands that worked.
中文：很多命令用非零退出码表示「答案」而不是「失败」：`grep` 没搜到返回 1，`diff` 有差异返回 1，`test` 为假返回 1。dsh 会把这类结果标成 `[exit code: 1]`
、卡片变红，系统提示词又要求模型「每个 bash 结果都检查 exit code，出错先排查」，于是模型反复重跑、核查，白白浪费轮次和 token。这个插件在结果里补一行说明，告诉模型这不是错误，可以
变红，系统提示词又要求模型「每个 bash 结果都检查 exit code，出错先排查」，于是模型反复重跑、核查，白白浪费轮次和 token。这个插件在结果里补一行说明，告诉模型这不是错误，可以继续。
## The problem
dsh's bash tool appends `[exit code: N]` to every non-zero result, and its system prompt says *"Chec
k the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on."* So when `
grep -rn TODO src` finds nothing, the model treats "no matches" as a failure and goes digging: re-ru
nning the search, listing directories, checking the file exists.

Community reports:
- Discussion #1884: a third-party eval where an exit-1 loop roughly doubled reque

sts (61 vs 32) on the same task.
- Discussion #8403: 7 of 56 tool results in one session were exit 1
, all from how the command was written, not real errors.
## What it does
After every `bash` call it checks the command and exit code. When the status is a known *answer*, it
adds one line above the marker:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The `[exit code: N]` marker stays the last line, so the terminal card still shows the exit pill. It
also adds one sentence to the system prompt so the model knows to trust the note.
Built-in rules (exit 1 only):
| Command | Meaning of exit 1 |

| `grep` `egrep` `fgrep` `zgrep` `rg` `ag` `ack` `git grep` | no matches |
| `diff` `cmp` `colordiff

` `git diff --exit-code/--quiet` | inputs differ |
| `test` `[` `[[` | condition is false |
| `which

` `type` `command -v/-V` `hash` | not installed |
| `pgrep` `pidof` | no such process |
| `git merge

-base --is-ancestor` | not an ancestor |
| `jq -e` (also `--exit-status`, combined flags like `-re`)

| last output false/null |
| `false` | always exits 1 |
Commands are matched by name, so full paths (`/usr/bin/grep`, `./node_modules/.bin/rg`) and quoted n
ames (`"grep"`) work. `git` global options before the subcommand (`-C dir`, `-c k=v`, `--no-pager`)
are skipped. Plain `git diff` (without `--exit-code`/`--quiet`) never exits 1 for changes, so it get
d. Plain `git diff` (without `--exit-code`/`--quiet`) never exits 1 for changes, so it gets no note.
## When it stays quiet

It is deliberately conservative. No note is added when:
- anything non-blank was written to stderr (

`grep pattern missing-file` exits 2 and prints an error — that *is* a failure);
- the exit code is a

nything other than the rule's code (e.g. `grep` 2, `diff` 2, 124 from `timeout`, 127 not found);
- t
he deciding command is not the last one: `grep x f | wc -l`, `grep x f; npm test`, `grep x f && npm

test`, `grep x f |& tee out`;
- the command contains `||` or a background `&` anywhere (`grep x f ||

echo none`, `cmd &`, `cmd & wait`);
- the command uses control flow or negation (`if`, `for`, `whil
e`, `case`, `function`, `!`), subshells, `{ …; }` groups or process substitution (`( … )`, `diff <(s

ort a) <(sort b)`), heredocs or here-strings (`<<EOF`, `<<<`), or has an unterminated quote;
- the d

eciding command runs through `xargs` (it maps child exit codes to 123);
- the call was killed, timed

out, failed to run, or the result has no `[exit code: N]` marker;
- the result already carries an `
[exit-code note: …]` line (it is never added twice).
Looked through, so the real command decides: leading `VAR=x` assignments, `env [-i] [VAR=x]`, `sudo`
/`doas` (flags without values, e.g. `-E`), `timeout [--signal=S | -s S | -k D] N`, `nice [-n N]`, `i
onice [-c N]`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `exec`, `stdbuf`, redirects anywhere in the command (`2>/
dev/null`, `>/dev/null 2>&1`, `&>out`, `< input`), trailing `# comments` and `\`-newline line contin
uations. `&&` and `||` inside `[[ … ]]` belong to the test, so `[[ -f a && -f b ]]` is treated as on
nd `||` inside `[[ … ]]` belong to the test, so `[[ -f a && -f b ]]` is treated as one `[[` command.
For a pipeline, or a command with an earlier `&&`/`;`/newline step (`cat log | grep x`, `cd src && g
rep …`), the note ends with "(Assuming the status came from the last command.)", because with `pipef
ail` or a failing earlier step the status could come from elsewhere.
## Install

Requires Node ≥ 24.9. Tested with dsh 0.2.1-rc.5. No build step, no runtime dependencies, no network
Node ≥ 24.9. Tested with dsh 0.2.1-rc.5. No build step, no runtime dependencies, no network access.
## Configure (optional)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`command` can be a name or a list of names (matched by basename, after the same look-through as buil
t-ins); `subcommand`, when set, must be the first argument; `{cmd}` and `{code}` in `note` become th
e command name and the exit code. The stay-quiet rules above apply to custom rules too. `prompt: fal
se` drops only the system-prompt sentence; results are still annotated.
## Cost
One extra line per matching result, and one sentence (~70 tokens) in the system prompt. The prompt s
entence is static, so it does not break the KV cache between requests. Set `prompt: false` to drop i
tence is static, so it does not break the KV cache between requests. Set `prompt: false` to drop it.
## Does it help? (measured)
We ran 4 tasks that lead the model into `grep`, `diff`, `git diff --exit-code` and `test -f` returni
ng 1, 3 times each, with and without the plugin, on DeepSeek's official API (2026-11-05):
| Model | Steps (off / on) | Tool calls (off / on) |

| `deepseek-flash` | 30 / 30 | 18 / 19 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | 24 / 24 | 12 / 12 |
[该节后续省略]
## What it does not do

- It does not hide the exit code or turn the card green. The model still sees the real status.
- It
does not cover PowerShell or Windows `cmd` yet.
